transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), Maya (NexaHead), Carlos (Security), Anita (PM), Samir (SRE).

Summary: quick scoping POC to align on success criteria and how NexaHealth's PHI/PII will be handled during the trial. Focus on logging, redaction, retention windows, prompt storage concerns for debugging + eval, and a 4-week timeline with an automated benchmark.

00:00:05 Jesse: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna run through what a typical POC looks like and specifically how we handle data. we have priya and liam from the eng side, i'll do the business side.
00:00:18 Maya: thanks, quick context — we're evaluating a hosted vs dedicated approach. primary constraint is PHI staying in our control, auditors want clear retention and redaction policies. goal is to prove inference latency and accuracy on our triage assistant.
00:00:32 Priya: great, the typical POC we do is 3-4 weeks. week 1 onboarding + security review, week 2 run benchmarks, week 3 iterate on prompts and redaction, week 4 finalize metrics and go/no-go. does that align with your timeline?
00:00:49 Anita: yes that's fine. main success criteria: p50 latency under 250ms for short responses, p95 under 700ms, and throughput targeted at ~40-60 req/s per model instance during peak. also need end-to-end correctness for redacted fields not appearing in outputs.
00:01:07 Liam: noted. for model choices we'll test one medium-sized open model and a quantized variant. for Redwood Dedicated we can pin capacity if you want reproducible throughput.
00:01:22 Carlos: security first — how do you handle logs? we cannot have raw PHI in logs, auditors will flag that.
00:01:29 Priya: understood. Redwood has multiple modes: full logging (for initial debug), redaction-on-ingress (automatic scrub of common PII patterns), and no-persist mode where prompts and responses are ephemeral and not stored. by default hosted keeps short retention for 30 days, dedicated can be configured to zero retention and send logs to your own S3 behind VPC.
00:01:51 Carlos: can the redaction run before any telemetry leaves our VPC? we prefer ingress-side redaction and then deliver only redacted text to your control plane.
00:01:58 Jesse: yes, for Private or VPC-deployed POCs we can run the redaction step in your environment. for hosted we provide client-side SDK hooks to run redaction locally before sending. we'll share a pattern and sample regexes.
00:02:12 Samir: timing — if we do redaction on the client it's extra latency. what's the ballpark?
00:02:18 Priya: typically redaction is a <20ms pre-processing step per request depending on complexity. in our benchmark plan we'll include both raw and redacted paths.
00:02:27 Maya: audit logs — we need tamper-evident audit logs and SSO integration. do you support SAML + SCIM?
00:02:33 Jesse: yes SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC at the token and route level, and audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM. we'll include an architecture note.
00:02:44 Carlos: KMS — keys must be customer-managed. how is encryption at rest handled?
00:02:49 Priya: we support customer KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated. hosted API supports bring-your-own-KMS for enterprise tiers; default is provider-managed encryption. we'll document the options and any additional attestations.
00:02:59 Anita: prompt storage is a concern for product because our prompts contain examples with PHI. we need to know who can access stored prompts for debugging and how long prompts are retained for eval.
00:03:09 Liam: internally we tag prompt artifacts and store them in a separate prompt-store. retention is configurable per-project: immediate deletion, 7d, 30d, or custom. access is restricted to roles. for audits we can produce an export that redacts tokens.
00:03:26 Carlos: can you do tokenization-based redaction so we never store the raw token sequence?
00:03:31 Priya: yes we support hashed or tokenized handles as an option; for debugging you can opt-in to share a redacted snapshot. by default redwood anonymizes PII patterns and strips identifiable tokens when configured.
00:03:44 Maya: what about debugging failures when we need full context? we may need to re-run with real data under a controlled setting.
00:03:50 Jesse: for those cases we propose ephemeral sessions: we can run a bounded test inside your VPC where nothing leaves the network and logs are stored to your S3 with lifecycle rules. Redwood engineers can be granted time-limited access via temporary credentials and everything is logged to your audit trail.
00:04:06 Samir: ok that addresses compliance concerns. benchmark specifics?
00:04:10 Priya: benchmark plan: 1) baseline functional check with a small sample set (1000 requests) to measure correctness and tokenization redaction; 2) load test ramp to target QPS (40-60) with 5-minute sustained windows to capture latency p50/p95/p99; 3) cold-start and KV-cache warmup runs to measure tail behavior; 4) end-to-end accuracy eval against your golden set.
00:04:35 Anita: what metrics do you collect out of the box?
00:04:38 Liam: per-request latency, tokens in/out, model variant, quantization profile, CPU/GPU utilization (if Dedicated), cache hit rates, and request sampling. we also export traces so you can join with your app logs.
00:04:50 Carlos: please ensure sampled request content in traces is redacted per our config.
00:04:53 Priya: yes sampling and redaction config are independent — you can sample full payloads but with automatic redaction applied, or sample only metadata.
00:05:04 Maya: success criteria recap — latency p50 <250ms, p95 <700ms, throughput 40-60 req/s, 0 leakage of PHI in outputs over 10k validation prompts.
00:05:16 Jesse: we'll aim for that, and we'll add a go/no-go checklist at the end of the POC.
00:05:22 Anita: contractually we need a short SOW that mentions retention SLAs for the POC and an NDA addendum allowing temporary access to data for debugging.
00:05:30 Jesse: we'll draft an SOW for a 4-week POC and share an NDA addendum template.
00:05:36 Carlos: one more question — do you persist KV caches or shards that might include prompt prefixes?
00:05:42 Priya: KV caches are ephemeral, held in-memory on the inference nodes; we do not persist KV caches to disk by default. if you want persisted caches for performance we can discuss encryption and access controls.
00:05:55 Samir: for throughput, are you suggesting burstable Dedicated or multiple pinned instances?
00:05:59 Liam: for predictable latency we recommend reserved instances (Dedicated) with autoscale buffers. for the POC we can start hosted with fixed concurrency to mimic dedicated behavior, then switch to Dedicated if we need exact matching.
00:06:12 Maya: costs — how will you estimate POC run costs?
00:06:16 Jesse: we'll provide a cost spreadsheet showing tokens, GPU hours for load tests, and optionally a reserved short-term Dedicated quote if you want pinned capacity for the benchmark day.
00:06:27 Anita: monitoring and trace retention — we need at least 90 days of trace metadata, but only 30 days of request payload retention. can those be decoupled?
00:06:36 Priya: yes metadata and payloads are decoupled in our system; retention windows can be set independently per-project.
00:06:44 Carlos: any compliance docs you can share immediately?
00:06:47 Jesse: we'll attach our SOC2 report, encryption whitepaper, and the POC SOW draft. expect that in email.
00:06:54 Maya: great. what's the immediate next step?
00:06:58 Jesse: action items: we'll send docs; you send a redacted sample and QPS profile; we'll lock a benchmark week of 12/8.
00:07:06 Anita: okay, thanks all.

(times later in call, conversation goes into some clarifications and small interruptions)

00:30:12 Carlos: quick note — our legal needs to see the exact retention settings UI because they want to ensure deletion is enforceable. is there a screenshot?
00:30:20 Jesse: yes we'll screenshot the console and show the API endpoint that deletes project data and returns a deletion token.
00:30:28 Samir: for the load test we'll provide a traffic profile that includes 5% large prompt cases to exercise tokenization and KV-cache behavior.
00:30:35 Priya: good idea, include long-context prompts to stress sequence-length handling.
00:30:42 Maya: do you support structured redaction rules (like remove any MRN or SSN formatted tokens) vs. regex only?
00:30:50 Liam: we support pattern libraries and custom NLP redactors that use entity recognition to find PHI. regex works for simple cases but NLP redactors are more robust.
00:30:58 Carlos: logging-level policy — we can't allow any developer access to raw request bodies in hosted mode. how does RBAC work?
00:31:05 Jesse: RBAC can restrict who can toggle retention settings and who can view sampled payloads. in hosted for enterprise customers we can gate developer-level access and require justification and time-limited approval.
00:31:18 Anita: will you provide an access log with user identities for every time someone views a sampled payload?
00:31:23 Liam: yes, access to sampled payloads is audited with identity, timestamp, and reason.
00:31:30 Carlos: timeline — can you get us a draft SOW and security bundle by next week?
00:31:35 Jesse: yes, we'll aim for EOD 2025-12-03.
00:31:40 Maya: thanks, we'll send sample data by 2025-12-02.
00:31:45 Jesse: perfect. any other competitors we should be aware you evaluated?
00:31:48 Anita: we looked briefly at Anthropic and some internal self-hosting recipes, but neither satisfied both latency and compliance together.
00:31:57 Jesse: understood. last bit — success criteria we will put into a short checklist and attach to the SOW.
00:32:03 Priya: and benchmark scripts, load generators, and redaction configs will be in a shared repo.
00:32:08 Jesse: okay thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and schedule.

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Redwood send SOC2 + security docs + demo console screenshots of retention UI.
- NexaHealth provide redacted sample dataset, QPS profile, and list of required PII fields to scrub.
- Priya/Liam to prepare benchmark plan and load scripts; schedule week of 2025-12-08 for running benchmarks.
- Jesse to draft 4-week SOW and NDA addendum and circulate by 2025-12-03.

End of transcript.
